title.en: Volume 274 Biographies 61: Yang Yongjian, Yao Diyu, Zhu Hongzuo, Wang Zhi, Song Luo, Chen Shen
title.raw: 卷274 列傳六十一 杨雍建 姚缔虞 朱宏祚 王隲 宋荦 陈诜

sentences.zh: 列傳六十一

translations.literal: Biographies 61
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 61

sentences.zh: 楊雍建姚締虞硃弘祚子綱王騭宋犖陳詵

translations.literal: Yang Yongjian, Yao Dingu, Zhu Hongzuo, Zigang, Wang Zhi, Song Luo, Chen Shen
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yongjian, Yao Dingu, Zhu Hongzuo, Zigang, Wang Zhi, Song Luo, and Chen Shen

sentences.zh: 楊雍建，字自西，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Yang Yongjian, whose style was Zixi, was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yongjian, styled Zixi, came from Haining in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，授廣東高耍知縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Gaoyao in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of Gaoyao in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時方用兵，總督駐高耍。

translations.literal: At the time military operations were under way, and the governor-general was stationed at Gaoyao.
translations.idiomatic: The province was at war, and the governor-general had his headquarters at Gaoyao.

sentences.zh: 師行徵民夫，吏慮其逃，縶之官廨。

translations.literal: When the army marched it conscripted laborers; clerks, fearing they would flee, bound them in the government compound.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the army marched it drafted laborers, and the clerks, fearing desertion, kept them shackled in the yamen.

sentences.zh: 當除夕，雍建命徙廊廡，撤餚饌畀之。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve Yongjian ordered them moved to the verandas and had the feast dishes taken out and given to them.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve he had them moved to the verandas and sent out the holiday feast for them to eat.

sentences.zh: 師中索榕樹枝製繩以燃砲，軍吏檄徵，語不遜，雍建笞之。

translations.literal: The army wanted banyan branches to make ropes for firing cannon; a military clerk issued a requisition with insolent language, and Yongjian had him flogged.
translations.idiomatic: The army demanded banyan branches to braid fuses for the guns; when a military clerk requisitioned them with insolent words, Yongjian had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 總督王國光以是稱雍建方剛，特疏薦。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wang Guoguang on this account praised Yongjian as upright and firm, and submitted a special memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wang Guoguang cited this as proof of Yongjian's firm integrity and memorialized the throne to recommend him specially.

sentences.zh: 蒞官甫一年，擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He had been in office barely a year when he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After barely a year in office he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，世祖幸南苑，雍建疏言：「昨因聖體違和，傳諭孟春饗太廟，遣官致祭。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year the Shizu Emperor visited the Southern Park; Yongjian submitted a memorial saying: "Yesterday, because the sacred person was unwell, an edict was issued that in early spring the Grand Temple would be feasted and officials dispatched to perform the sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year the Shizu Emperor visited the Southern Park, and Yongjian memorialized: "Yesterday, because Your Majesty was unwell, an edict announced that the spring sacrifice at the Grand Temple would be performed by dispatched officials."

sentences.zh: 至期皇躬康豫，仍親廟祀，此敬修祀典之盛心也。

translations.literal: When the day came the imperial person was restored to health and still personally performed the temple sacrifice—this was the great mind devoted to reverently maintaining the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came Your Majesty had recovered and still went in person to the temple—proof of how earnestly you honor the ritual calendar.

sentences.zh: 乃回宮未幾，复幸南苑，寒威未釋，陟歷郊原，恐不足以慎起居。

translations.literal: Yet scarcely after returning to the palace he again visited the Southern Park; the cold force had not yet lifted, and to climb and traverse the suburban wilds— I fear this is not sufficient for careful attention to daily regimen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet hardly back at the palace you have returned to the Southern Park; the cold has not yet broken, and to roam the open countryside may not be prudent for Your Majesty's health.

sentences.zh: 且古者蒐苗狝狩，各有其時。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity the spring review, summer hunt, autumn battue, and winter hunt each had its season.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, in antiquity the spring muster, summer hunt, autumn battue, and winter chase each had its proper season.

sentences.zh: 設使獸起於前，馬逸於後，驚屬車之清塵，豈能無萬一之慮？

translations.literal: Suppose a beast should start up ahead and a horse bolt behind— startling the clear dust of the attendant chariots— could there be no thought of the slightest mishap?
translations.idiomatic: If a beast should spring up ahead or a horse bolt behind and startle the imperial train, can there be no fear of the slightest accident?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上甚怒，宣雍建入，諭以閱兵習武之意。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angered and summoned Yongjian in, instructing him of the intent to review troops and practice martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived the emperor was furious and had Yongjian brought in to explain that the visit was for troop review and martial training.

sentences.zh: 雍建奏對不失常度，上意亦解。

translations.literal: Yongjian answered at court without losing his usual composure, and the emperor's mind was also eased.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjian answered without losing his composure, and the emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 時平南王尚可喜、靖南王耿繼茂並鎮廣東，雍建疏陳廣東害民之政八：委吏太濫，雜派太繁，裡役無定例，用夫無定制，鹽埠日橫，私稅日盈，伐薪採木，大肆流毒，均宜亟為革除。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi and the Prince of Jingnan Geng Jimao both garrisoned Guangdong; Yongjian memorialized eight policies in Guangdong that harmed the people: delegated clerks too numerous, miscellaneous levies too complex, village corvée without fixed rules, labor requisition without fixed regulations, salt depots growing daily overbearing, private taxes daily increasing, cutting firewood and gathering timber spreading great harm—all should urgently be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, and the Prince of Jingnan, Geng Jimao, both held Guangdong; Yongjian listed eight abuses there: too many delegated clerks, too many miscellaneous levies, village corvée without fixed rules, labor drafts without fixed quotas, salt monopolies growing more oppressive by the day, private taxes mounting daily, and timber-cutting spreading misery everywhere—all of which should be abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 且兩籓並建，供億維繁。

translations.literal: Moreover, with both princely establishments erected, provisioning was extremely burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: With both princely establishments in place, provisioning the court had become crushing.

sentences.zh: 今川、貴底定，請移一籓鎮撫其地，俾粵民甦息。

translations.literal: Now that Sichuan and Guizhou are settled, he asked that one princedom be moved to garrison and pacify those regions, so that the people of Guangdong might revive and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Sichuan and Guizhou were pacified, he asked that one princedom be transferred to garrison there so the people of Guangdong could breathe again.

sentences.zh: 上尋命繼茂移鎮福建，雍建發之也。

translations.literal: The emperor soon ordered Jimao to transfer his garrison to Fujian—this was set in motion by Yongjian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon ordered Geng Jimao to transfer his garrison to Fujian—Yongjian had set this in motion.

sentences.zh: 十七年，疏言：「朋黨之患，釀於草野。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he memorialized: "The affliction of faction arises and ferments in the countryside."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he memorialized: "The scourge of faction begins in the countryside."

sentences.zh: 欲塞其源，宜嚴禁盟社，請飭學臣查禁。

translations.literal: To block its source, alliance societies should be strictly forbidden; he asked that educational commissioners be ordered to investigate and ban them.
translations.idiomatic: To cut it off at the source, alliance societies should be strictly banned, and he asked that the educational commissioners be ordered to investigate and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved his request.

sentences.zh: 轉吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，輔臣秉政，奏事者入見，皆長跪，雍建獨立語。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Ancestor took the throne, assisting ministers held power; those who came to report affairs all knelt long, but Yongjian alone stood and spoke.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor ascended the throne, the regents held power; everyone who came to report affairs knelt, but Yongjian alone stood and spoke.

sentences.zh: 比退，輔臣目之曰：「此南苑上書諫獵者也。

translations.literal: When he withdrew, an assisting minister eyed him and said: "This is the one who at the Southern Park submitted a memorial admonishing the hunt."
translations.idiomatic: As he left, a regent eyed him and said, "That is the man who memorialized against the hunt at the Southern Park."

sentences.zh: 」自是奏事者見輔臣皆不跪。

translations.literal: " From then on those who reported affairs did not kneel when they saw assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on officials reporting to the regents no longer knelt.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，彗星見。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kangxi a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 雍建奏言：「天心仁愛，垂象示警。

translations.literal: Yongjian memorialized: "Heaven's mind is benevolent; it displays signs to give warning."
translations.idiomatic: Yongjian memorialized: "Heaven is benevolent; it sends omens as a warning."

sentences.zh: 乞齋心修省，廣求直言，詳詢利病，並飭內外臣工，滌慮洗心，共修職業，」上優旨褒答。

translations.literal: He begged purification of mind and self-examination, broad solicitation of blunt speech, detailed inquiry into benefits and harms, and also ordered inner and outer officials to cleanse thoughts and hearts and together cultivate their duties." The emperor replied with an excellent edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor to purify his mind and examine himself, to seek blunt counsel widely, to inquire into what helps and harms the realm, and to order officials everywhere to clear their minds and devote themselves to duty." The emperor answered with a gracious edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「治化未醇，由於臣職未盡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized: "Governance and transformation are not yet pure because ministers' duties are not fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he memorialized: "Good government has not yet matured because officials are not doing their jobs."

sentences.zh: 比者部臣以推諉為卸責，明為本部應議之事，或請諮別部，或請飭督撫，致一案之處分，因一人之口供未到而更待另議；

translations.literal: Recently ministry officials take shirking as unloading responsibility: matters clearly belonging to their own ministry for deliberation they either ask to consult another ministry or ask to order governors-general and governors, so that disposition of a case, because one person's testimony has not yet arrived, must again await separate deliberation;
translations.idiomatic: Lately ministry officials treat buck-passing as discharge of duty: matters plainly within their own jurisdiction they refer to other ministries or to the governors, so that a case cannot be decided because one witness has not yet testified;

sentences.zh: 一事之行止，因一時文卷小誤而重俟行查；

translations.literal: whether a matter proceeds or stops, because of a momentary small error in documents, again awaits investigation;
translations.idiomatic: whether a matter proceeds or stalls because of a minor clerical error, they order yet another review;

sentences.zh: 至地方利弊所關，憚於釐正，輒云已經題定，無庸再議。

translations.literal: as for what concerns local benefits and harms, fearing to rectify they always say it has already been memorialized and fixed, with no need to deliberate again.
translations.idiomatic: and when local abuses are at stake they shrink from reform, saying the matter was already settled and need not be reopened.

sentences.zh: 如此，則一二胥吏執定例以駁之足矣，不知滿、漢堂司各官所司為何事也。

translations.literal: If it is like this, then one or two clerks holding fixed precedents to rebut matters would suffice— one does not know what the Manchu and Han directors and section chiefs of each ministry are charged with.
translations.idiomatic: At this rate a couple of clerks citing precedent could run the ministries, and one wonders what the Manchu and Han directors are for.

sentences.zh: 督撫以蒙蔽為苟安，民苦於差徭，而額外之私徵，未聞建長策以除積困；

translations.literal: governors-general and governors take concealment as temporary peace; the people suffer from corvée and levies, yet extra private exactions— no long-term policy is heard proposed to remove accumulated distress;
translations.idiomatic: Governors treat concealment as peace; the people groan under corvée and levies while extra private exactions go unchecked, and no one proposes a lasting remedy for these chronic ills;

sentences.zh: 吏橫於貪暴，而有司之掊克，不過摘薄罪以引輕條。

translations.literal: clerks are overbearing in greed and violence, yet when superiors extort, they only pick out minor offenses to invoke light statutes.
translations.idiomatic: subordinates run wild in greed and violence, yet when superiors are caught extorting they are charged only with minor offenses under the lightest statutes.

sentences.zh: 向日行考滿之法，則題報者皆稱職，曾無三等以下之劣員；

translations.literal: when the former triennial evaluation was carried out, those reported were all called competent, and never was there an inferior official below the third grade;
translations.idiomatic: Under the triennial evaluation every reported official was rated competent, and never once was anyone graded below the third rank;

sentences.zh: 平時上彈劾之章，則特糾者僅末僚，不及道府以上之大吏。

translations.literal: in ordinary times when impeachment memorials were submitted, those specially impeached were only low subordinates, not reaching great officials at the circuit and prefectural level and above.
translations.idiomatic: and when impeachments were filed they targeted only junior clerks, never circuit intendants, prefects, or higher officials.

sentences.zh: 凡此推諉蒙蔽之習，請嚴飭內外臣工各圖報稱，儻仍蹈故轍，立予罷斥，以儆官常。

translations.literal: All these habits of shirking and concealment— he asked that inner and outer officials be strictly ordered each to plan repayment of favor; if they still tread the old rut, immediately dismiss them, to warn official norms.
translations.idiomatic: For all these habits of buck-passing and cover-up, he asked that officials everywhere be strictly ordered to earn their keep; anyone who persists in the old ways should be dismissed at once as a warning to the service.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was reported.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was received and noted.

sentences.zh: 尋自刑科都給事中累擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: Soon from chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of Punishments he was repeatedly promoted to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose from chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十八年，典會試，授貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he presided over the metropolitan examination and was appointed governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he presided over the metropolitan examination and was appointed governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 疏請立營製，減徭役，招集流亡，禁革私派。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to establish camp regulations, reduce corvée and levies, gather displaced persons, and forbid and abolish private levies.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to establish garrison regulations, reduce corvée, recall refugees, and abolish unauthorized levies.

sentences.zh: 土司謁巡撫，故事，必鳴鼓角，交戟於門，俾拜其下。

translations.literal: When native chieftains called on the governor, by precedent drums and horns were sounded and halberds crossed at the gate, making them bow below.
translations.idiomatic: When native chieftains came to call on the governor, custom required drums and horns and crossed halberds at the gate, forcing them to prostrate themselves outside.

sentences.zh: 雍建悉屏去，引至座前問疾苦，予以酒食，土司咸輸服。

translations.literal: Yongjian removed all of these entirely, led them before his seat to ask their hardships, and gave them wine and food; the native chieftains all submitted in conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjian abolished all of this, brought them before his desk to ask after their hardships, and gave them food and wine; the chieftains were won over completely.

sentences.zh: 始，貴陽斗米值錢五千，雍建請轉餉以給。

translations.literal: At first a dou of rice in Guiyang was worth five thousand cash; Yongjian asked to transfer grain rations to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: At first a dou of rice in Guiyang cost five thousand cash; Yongjian requested grain shipments from elsewhere to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 既，令民翦荒茅，教以耕種。

translations.literal: Afterward he ordered the people to cut wild thatch and taught them to plow and plant.
translations.idiomatic: Then he had the people clear the wild scrub and taught them how to farm.

sentences.zh: 比三年，稻田日闢，民食以裕。

translations.literal: By the third year paddy fields were daily expanded and the people's food thereby became ample.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years paddy fields spread steadily and the people had enough to eat.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，召授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was summoned and appointed vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was recalled to the capital and appointed vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋以親老乞終養，許之。

translations.literal: Soon, because his parents were aged, he begged to retire and care for them until their end; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing aged parents, he asked to retire and care for them at home, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he died, and sacrificial burial was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he died, and the court granted him a state funeral.

sentences.zh: 子中訥，進士，官右中允。

translations.literal: His son Zhongne was a jinshi and served as right attendant in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongne, a jinshi, served as right attendant in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 姚締虞，字歷升，湖廣黃陂人。

translations.literal: Yao Dingu, whose style was Lisheng, was a native of Huangpi in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Dingu, styled Lisheng, came from Huangpi in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士，授四川成都府推官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating censor of Chengdu Prefecture in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi and was appointed investigating censor of Chengdu Prefecture in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四川殘民多聚為盜，互告訐，釀大獄。

translations.literal: In Sichuan many remnant people gathered as bandits, mutually informing and impeaching, brewing great cases.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan many survivors of the wars had turned bandit; mutual accusations bred major prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 締虞平恕讞鞫，輒得其情，審釋叛案株連獄囚十七人。

translations.literal: Dingu was even and lenient in judging and interrogating, always obtaining the true circumstances, and on examination released seventeen prisoners implicated in a rebellion case.
translations.idiomatic: Dingu judged cases with calm fairness and always got to the truth; he reviewed a treason case and released seventeen prisoners caught in its dragnet.

sentences.zh: 總督苗澄、巡撫張德地薦廉能，舉卓異，會裁缺，改陝西安化知縣。

translations.literal: Governor-General Miao Cheng and Governor Zhang Dedi recommended him as incorrupt and capable and nominated him for outstanding merit; when posts were cut he was transferred to magistrate of Anhua in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Miao Cheng and Governor Zhang Dedi recommended him as incorrupt and capable and rated him outstanding; when posts were cut he was reassigned as magistrate of Anhua in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 行取，康熙十五年，授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: Selected for capital service, in the fifteenth year of Kangxi he was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for service in the capital, in the fifteenth year of Kangxi he was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 疏請嚴選庶吉士，考覈翰林，報聞。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking for strict selection of Hanlin bachelors and examination of the Hanlin Academy; acknowledgment was reported.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for stricter selection of Hanlin bachelors and tighter review of the Academy; the memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 十七年，典試江西，還，奏：「江西被賊殘破州縣在丁缺田荒案內者，請敕督撫酌量輕重，限三年或五年勸墾，以漸昇科。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he presided over the provincial examination in Jiangxi; on returning he memorialized: "Jiangxi counties ravaged by bandits that fall within cases of missing population registers and abandoned fields— please order governors-general and governors to weigh severity, set a limit of three or five years to encourage cultivation, and gradually restore taxation."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, after presiding over the Jiangxi provincial examination, he reported: "For counties in Jiangxi ruined by rebels and listed under missing registers and abandoned fields, order the governors to set a three- or five-year limit for bringing land back under cultivation before taxes resume."

sentences.zh: 全省逋賦二百二十萬，歷年追比，僅報完三萬。

translations.literal: The whole province's arrears in tax amounted to 2,200,000; pursued year after year, only 30,000 was reported completed.
translations.idiomatic: The province owed 2.2 million taels in back taxes; after years of relentless collection only 30,000 had been reported paid.

sentences.zh: 此二百十餘萬，雖敲骨吸髓，勢必不能復完。

translations.literal: These more than 2,100,000— even if bones were knocked and marrow sucked, they inevitably could not be completed again.
translations.idiomatic: That remaining 2.1 million could never be collected even if the people were squeezed dry.

sentences.zh: 請早予蠲免，俾小民得免死亡。

translations.literal: He asked that remission be granted early, so that common people might escape death.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that it be remitted soon so the common people would not die under the burden.

sentences.zh: 十八年，地震，求言。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year there was an earthquake, and blunt counsel was sought.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year an earthquake struck, and the court called for candid advice.

sentences.zh: 締虞上疏曰：「科道乃朝廷耳目之官，原期知無不言，有聞則告。

translations.literal: Dingu submitted a memorial saying: "The censorate and supervising secretaries are the court's eyes and ears; originally it was expected that what they knew they would not fail to speak, and what they heard they would report."
translations.idiomatic: Dingu memorialized: "The censorate and supervising secretaries are the court's eyes and ears; they are meant to speak of whatever they know and report whatever they hear."

sentences.zh: 自故憲臣艾元徵請禁風聞條奏，自此言路氣靡，中外多所顧忌。

translations.literal: Since the late censor Ai Yuanzheng asked to forbid memorials based on hearsay, from then the avenue of speech wilted in spirit, and inside and outside there were many scruples.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the late censor Ai Yuanzheng asked to ban memorials based on hearsay, the avenue of remonstrance has withered and officials everywhere have grown cautious.

sentences.zh: 臣請皇上省覽世祖朝諸臣奏議，如何謇諤；

translations.literal: Your servant asks Your Majesty to review the memorials and deliberations of officials in the Shizu reign— how outspoken they were;
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to read the memorials of the Shunzhi reign and see how blunt officials once were;

sentences.zh: 今者相率以條陳為事，輭熟成風。

translations.literal: now they lead one another in making itemized submissions their business, and soft complacency has become the fashion.
translations.idiomatic: whereas now everyone files routine bulletins and a culture of smooth complacency has taken hold.

sentences.zh: 蓋平時無以作其敢言之氣，一旦欲其慷慨直陳，難矣。

translations.literal: For in ordinary times nothing is done to rouse their spirit of daring speech; once you wish them to speak forthrightly and plainly, it is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: For if nothing in ordinary times encourages them to speak boldly, you cannot expect frank counsel on demand.

sentences.zh: 乞敕廷臣會議，嗣後有矢志忠誠、指斥奸佞者，即少差謬，亦賜矜全。

translations.literal: He begged that court ministers be ordered to confer: hereafter if there are those who set their hearts on loyalty and denounce the treacherous and corrupt, even if slightly in error, still grant them compassionate forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to deliberate: hereafter officials who speak in loyal earnest against corruption, even if slightly mistaken, should be treated with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 如或快意恩仇，受人指使，章奏鈔傳，眾目難掩，縱令彈劾得實，亦難免於徇私之罪。

translations.literal: If they gratify private enmity, accept another's direction, circulate memorial copies, and many eyes cannot conceal it— even if impeachment is substantiated, they still cannot escape the crime of partiality.
translations.idiomatic: But if they settle private scores, take orders from others, and circulate their memorials so that everyone sees, then even a substantiated impeachment will still be punished as self-serving.

sentences.zh: 如此，則言官有所顧忌，不敢妄言；

translations.literal: In this way remonstrating officials would have scruples and not speak rashly;
translations.idiomatic: That way remonstrating officials would have reason to be careful and not speak rashly;

sentences.zh: 中外諸臣有所顧忌，不敢妄為。

translations.literal: and officials inside and outside would have scruples and not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: and officials everywhere would think twice before acting rashly.

sentences.zh: 」疏下九卿科道會議。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the Nine Ministers and the censorate for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the Nine Ministers and the censorate for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 越日，召廷臣等集中左門，上問：「締虞疏如何定議？

translations.literal: The next day court ministers were summoned to assemble at the Left Gate; the emperor asked: "How is Dingu's memorial to be decided?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor summoned the ministers to the Left Gate and asked, "How do you rule on Dingu's memorial?"

sentences.zh: 」吏部尚書郝惟訥等暨給事中李宗孔等俱言風聞之例，不宜復開。

translations.literal: " Minister of Personnel Hao Weine and others together with supervising secretary Li Zongkong and others all said the precedent on hearsay should not be reopened.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Personnel Hao Weine, supervising secretary Li Zongkong, and others all said the ban on hearsay memorials should not be lifted.

sentences.zh: 上問：「締虞，爾意如何？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Dingu, what is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Dingu, what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」締虞對曰：「皇上明聖，從未譴罪言官。

translations.literal: " Dingu answered: "Your Majesty is enlightened and sage and has never punished remonstrating officials."
translations.idiomatic: " Dingu answered, "Your Majesty is enlightened and has never punished a remonstrating official."

sentences.zh: 但有處分條例在，言官皆生畏懼。

translations.literal: But because disciplinary regulations exist, remonstrating officials all grow fearful.
translations.idiomatic: But the disciplinary regulations still exist, and that makes remonstrating officials afraid.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「如汝言，條例便當廢耶？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "As you say, should the regulations then be abolished?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "So by your logic the regulations should be abolished?"

sentences.zh: 」締虞對曰：「科條雖設，當辨公私誠偽。

translations.literal: " Dingu answered: "Though the statutes are established, public and private sincerity and falsity should be distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: " Dingu answered, "The statutes may remain, but each case should be judged on whether the speaker acted from public duty or private motive."

sentences.zh: 」上意稍解。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's anger eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 諭言：「官宜敷陳國家大事，如有大奸大貪，糾劾得實，法在必行，決不姑貸。

translations.literal: An instruction was issued: "Officials should set forth great affairs of state; if there are great traitors or great greed and impeachment is substantiated, the law must be enforced and will never be indulgently spared."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed them: "Officials should speak frankly on affairs of state; when great traitors or great corruption are exposed and the charges are proved, the law will be enforced without mercy."

sentences.zh: 且魏象樞彈奏程汝璞，亦是風聞，已鞫問得實，原未嘗有風聞之禁也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Wei Xiangshu impeached Cheng Rupu, that too was based on hearsay; after interrogation it was substantiated— originally there never was a ban on hearsay.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Xiangshu impeached Cheng Rupu it was also on hearsay, yet investigation proved the charge— there never was a true ban on hearsay memorials.

sentences.zh: 」上宣締虞前，指內閣所呈世祖時章奏示之曰：「汝以朕為未閱此乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned Dingu forward, pointed to memorials from the Shizu reign presented by the Grand Secretariat, and showed them, saying: "Do you think We have not read these?"
translations.idiomatic: " He had Dingu brought forward, pointed to Shunzhi-era memorials from the Grand Secretariat, and said, "Do you think I have not read these?"

sentences.zh: 」締虞對曰：「惟久經聖覽，臣故不憚盡言。

translations.literal: " Dingu answered: "Precisely because they have long been perused by Your sagely gaze, your servant therefore does not fear to speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: " Dingu answered, "Because Your Majesty has long read them, I did not hesitate to speak plainly."

sentences.zh: 」上命以所言宣付史館。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered that what had been said be proclaimed and sent to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered his words recorded and sent to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 次日，復命締虞入起居注，授筆札記之。

translations.literal: The next day Dingu was again ordered to enter the Diary of Activity and Repose and was given brush and paper to record it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Dingu was again summoned to the Diary of Activity and Repose and given brush and paper to write the record.

sentences.zh: 尋轉工科掌印給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to supervising secretary with seal in the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 上考察科道，黜孫緒極、傅廷俊、和鹽鼎三人，而嘉締虞與王曰溫、李迥稱職。

translations.literal: The emperor examined the censorate and dismissed Sun Juji, Fu Tingjun, and He Yanding— three men— while praising Dingu together with Wang Yuewen and Li Jiong as competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reviewed the censorate he dismissed Sun Juji, Fu Tingjun, and He Yanding, but praised Dingu along with Wang Yuewen and Li Jiong as competent officials.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，疏論外吏積習，視事偷惰，公務沉閣，文移遲緩；

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he memorialized on the accumulated habits of outer officials: attending to duties with lazy theft, public business sunk in files, documents delayed;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he memorialized on the bad habits of provincial officials: neglecting their duties, letting business pile up, and delaying documents;

sentences.zh: 僚屬宴會，遊客酬酢，廢時糜費。

translations.literal: subordinates feasting, travelers exchanging toasts, wasting time and squandering expense.
translations.idiomatic: holding banquets for staff and visitors, wasting time and money on entertainment.

sentences.zh: 請敕部禁飭。

translations.literal: He asked that ministries be ordered to forbid and correct this.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the ministries to forbid these practices.

sentences.zh: 累擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授四川巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed governor of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 締虞先為推官有聲，百姓喜其來。

translations.literal: Dingu had earlier won renown as investigating censor, and the common people rejoiced at his coming.
translations.idiomatic: Dingu had already won fame as investigating censor there, and the people rejoiced at his return.

sentences.zh: 締虞至，榜上諭於廳事，嚴約束，禁私徵雜派，杜絕餽遺，屬吏憚之。

translations.literal: When Dingu arrived he posted a proclamation in the hall announcing strict constraints, forbidding private levies and miscellaneous exactions, cutting off gifts entirely; subordinate officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingu arrived he posted strict rules in the yamen hall, banned unauthorized levies and gifts, and his subordinates were afraid of him.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「四川迭經兵火，荒殘已極。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Sichuan has suffered repeated warfare by fire, and desolation has reached its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Sichuan has been ravaged by war after war until the land lies in utter ruin.

sentences.zh: 官戶鄉紳，多流寓外省，雖令子弟復業，迨入學鄉舉登仕版後，仍棄本籍他往。

translations.literal: Official households and village gentry for the most part sojourned in other provinces; though they were ordered to send sons to return to their estates, once the sons entered schools, won degrees in local examinations, and had their names placed on the roster of office, they still abandoned their original registers and went elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Official households and local gentry had mostly fled to other provinces; even when they sent sons back to reclaim the family estate, once those sons entered school, passed the provincial exams, and were posted to office they again abandoned their native register and left.

sentences.zh: 百姓見其如此，亦裹足不歸。

translations.literal: The common people, seeing this, also bound their feet and would not return.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this, commoners too held back and would not return home.

sentences.zh: 若招回鄉宦一家，可抵百姓數戶。

translations.literal: If one could summon back a single family of returned gentry, it could equal several commoner households.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling one gentry family to the countryside was worth as much as summoning back several dozen commoner households.

sentences.zh: 紳宦既歸，百姓亦不招而自至。

translations.literal: Once the gentry had returned, the common people likewise came without being summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Once the gentry returned, commoners arrived on their own without needing to be called.

sentences.zh: 今察明各屬流寓外省紳衿，請敕部移行，飭令復業。

translations.literal: Now having ascertained each jurisdiction's gentry scholars sojourning in other provinces, he asked that the ministry be ordered to circulate documents and command them to return to their estates.
translations.idiomatic: Having identified the gentry-scholars from each district who were living abroad, he asked that orders be sent through the ministries commanding them to resume their occupations at home.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 蜀人困於採木，締虞陛辭，首陳其害。

translations.literal: The people of Shu were afflicted by timber-cutting levies; at his audience of farewell Dingu first stated the harms.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were exhausted by timber-cutting labor; when Dingu took leave of the throne at court he was the first to describe the harm.

sentences.zh: 會鬆威道王騭入覲，亦舉是以奏，詔特免之。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Zhi of the Songwei Circuit came to court for audience and likewise memorialized on this matter; an edict specially exempted them.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Wang Zhi of Songwei Circuit came to audience at court and memorialized on the same grounds; the emperor commanded a special exemption.

sentences.zh: 復請免運白蠟，停解鐵稅，皆獲施行。

translations.literal: He again requested exemption from transport of white wax and cessation of iron tax delivery; all were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to end the transport of white wax and the delivery of iron taxes, and all these measures were carried out.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒官，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died in office and was granted sacrificial burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died in office and was granted funeral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 硃弘祚，字徽廕，山東高唐人，昌祚弟。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzuo, styled Huiyin, was a man of Gaotang in Shandong, younger brother of Changzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzuo, styled Huiyin, came from Gaotang in Shandong and was the younger brother of Changzuo.

sentences.zh: 弘祚自舉人授江南盱眙知縣，有惠政，舉卓異。

translations.literal: Hongzuo from juren was appointed magistrate of Xuyi in Jiangnan; he had benevolent administration and was recommended as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving his juren degree Hongzuo was appointed magistrate of Xuyi in Jiangnan; his humane governance won him recommendation as outstanding.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，行取御史，以昌祚子紱官大理寺卿迴避，改刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi he was selected by promotion to investigating censor, but because Changzuo's son Fu held the post of vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review he had to avoid conflict and was changed to a clerkship in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi he was tapped for promotion to investigating censor, but had to decline because Changzuo's son Fu was vice minister of the Dali Court; he was reassigned as a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 再遷兵部督捕郎中，出為直隸天津道僉事，調直隸守道參議。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to bureau director in the Ministry of War supervising arrests, then went out as assistant commissioner of the Tianjin Circuit in Zhili, and was transferred to the Defender Circuit of Zhili as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising-arrests director in the Ministry of War, then sent out as assistant commissioner on the Tianjin Circuit in Zhili and later transferred to vice commissioner on the Defender Circuit of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，超擢廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was extraordinarily promoted to governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted ahead of schedule to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 入見，奏對稱旨，賜帑金千，及內廝鞍馬。

translations.literal: On entering audience his memorial replies pleased the emperor, who bestowed a thousand taels from the privy purse and palace eunuch saddles and horses.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience his answers pleased the throne; he received a thousand taels from the imperial treasury and saddled horses from the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 過庾嶺，察知夫役苦累，首禁革之。

translations.literal: Passing the Dayu Ridge he perceived the bitter burdens on coolie labor and was the first to forbid and abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Dayu Pass he saw how corvée porters suffered and was the first to ban the practice.

sentences.zh: 复牒兵部，凡使者過境，有驛站供億，不得更有所役。

translations.literal: He again sent a dispatch to the Ministry of War: whenever envoys passed through a district the post stations should provide supplies and no further labor might be demanded.
translations.idiomatic: He also notified the Ministry of War that traveling envoys must rely on postal stations for provisions and must not levy additional labor.

sentences.zh: 廣東軍興後，無藝之徵，浮於正供，悉罷免。

translations.literal: After Guangdong's military campaigns, levies without statutory basis exceeded the regular tax quota; he abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars in Guangdong, unauthorized levies had piled above the regular taxes; he abolished them all.

sentences.zh: 劾墨吏尤者數人，餘悉奉法。

translations.literal: He impeached the worst corrupt clerks, several persons; the rest all observed the law.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the worst corrupt clerks and the rest fell into line with the law.

sentences.zh: 鹽法為籓下奸民所亂，據引地莫敢譙訶。

translations.literal: The salt regulations were thrown into disorder by scoundrels under the princely establishment; they held the license districts and none dared denounce them.
translations.idiomatic: Rascals attached to the princely fief had wrecked the salt trade, monopolizing licensed districts so that no one dared complain.

sentences.zh: 弘祚疏陳整飭鹽政數事，如議行。

translations.literal: Hongzuo memorialized enumerating several matters for rectifying salt administration, and they were enacted as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo memorialized reforms to restore the salt administration, and they were carried out as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 高州屬縣吳川，瓊州屬縣臨高、澄邁，戶少田蕪，積逋十二萬兩有奇，疏請豁免。

translations.literal: Wuchuan in Gaozhou, Lin'gao and Chengmai in Qiongzhou—all had few households and fallow fields, with accumulated arrears of more than one hundred and twenty thousand taels; he memorialized requesting exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchuan under Gaozhou and Lin'gao and Chengmai under Qiongzhou had few households and abandoned fields, with more than 120,000 taels in arrears; he memorialized for their remission.

sentences.zh: 衛所屯田歲輸糧三斗，額重多逃亡。

translations.literal: Garrison farmlands at military colonies paid three dou of grain yearly; the quota was heavy and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: Military colony lands paid three dou of grain per year—a burden so heavy that many peasants fled.

sentences.zh: 弘祚言：「民糧重，則每畝八升八合起科，今屯田浮三之二，非卹兵之道，當比例裁減。

translations.literal: Hongzuo said: "When civilian grain tax is heavy, collection begins at eight sheng eight he per mou; now military colony land is more than two-thirds above that—this is not the way to pity the troops; it should be proportionally reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo said: "Regular farmland is taxed at eight sheng eight he per mou; military colony lands are taxed two-thirds higher—not a humane policy for the soldiers and should be reduced in proportion.

sentences.zh: 」事皆允行。

translations.literal: " All requests were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 逆亂方定，奸民告訐無已，疏請嚴妄首株連之例，略謂：「當定南分鎮，聞風投冒倚藉聲勢者，實繁有徒，迨經平定，籓下人應歸旗者，悉已簿錄解京；

translations.literal: The rebellion had just been pacified and malicious persons lodged accusations without end; he memorialized asking for strict enforcement of rules against false accusers and guilt by association, saying in summary: "When the pacification of the South was set up, those who heard the wind and rushed to attach themselves by borrowing others' prestige were indeed numerous; after pacification those under the princely establishment who should return to the banners had all been registered and sent to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion freshly suppressed, informers kept filing endless accusations; he asked for strict penalties on false accusers and collective punishment, writing in part: "When the southern pacification commissioner was first established, countless people rushed to claim ties to the rebellion and borrow its prestige; after order was restored those under the princely banner who should return to the Eight Banners had all been registered and sent to Beijing;

sentences.zh: 籍內無名者，釋放為民。

translations.literal: those not named in the registers were released as civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone not listed in the registers was released as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 嗣有旨：'籓下官兵、奴僕及貿易人等，除實係遼東舊人及價買人外，逐一清查，發出為民。

translations.literal: Subsequently there was an edict: 'Princely troops, servants, and traders—except those who were truly old inhabitants of Liaodong or purchased persons—are to be examined case by case and released as civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict declared: "Troops, servants, and traders under the princely establishment—except true Liaodong natives or legally purchased bondservants—must be examined one by one and released to civilian status.

sentences.zh: '臣尋繹詔意，原以諸人皆朝廷赤子，不忍株累。

translations.literal: The minister traced the meaning of the edict: originally all these people were the red children of the court, and the throne could not bear to implicate them collectively.
translations.idiomatic: I followed the intent of that edict: these people were all subjects of the Son of Heaven, and the court did not wish to punish them collectively.

sentences.zh: 且十餘年來，或補伍，或歸農，或死亡遷徙，無籍可稽。

translations.literal: Moreover, over more than ten years some had joined the ranks, some returned to farming, some died or moved away—with no register that could be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than a decade many had joined garrison units, returned to farming, died, or moved away, leaving no records to verify.

sentences.zh: 乃姦宄之徒，蔓引株連，或在部呈首，或向有司告訐；

translations.literal: Yet wicked persons extended accusations and dragged others in by association, some presenting charges at the ministry, some informing before local officials;
translations.idiomatic: Yet scoundrels kept expanding accusations and implicating others, filing charges at the ministries or before local officials;

sentences.zh: 及事白省釋，而官民之被累已深。

translations.literal: and by the time matters were cleared and persons released, officials and commoners had already suffered deep injury.
translations.idiomatic: By the time cases were cleared and prisoners released, officials and commoners had already suffered severe harm.

sentences.zh: 請敕部嚴議。

translations.literal: He asked that the ministries be ordered to deliberate strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the ministries be ordered to enact strict rules.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，擢福建浙江總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 值大計，弘祚疏言「福建地瘠民佻」，上責弘祚失言，謂：「賢才不擇地而生。

translations.literal: At the great evaluation Hongzuo memorialized "Fujian's land is poor and its people frivolous"; the emperor reproached Hongzuo for impropriety of speech, saying: "Talents and worthies are not choosy about where they are born.
translations.idiomatic: During the great evaluation Hongzuo memorialized that "Fujian's soil is poor and its people frivolous." The emperor rebuked him for improper speech, saying: "Talent is not born only in fertile lands.

sentences.zh: 四川巡撫張德地署延綏巡撫，言'延綏邊地，無可舉博學鴻詞者'；

translations.literal: Zhang Dedi, governor of Sichuan, while acting as governor of Yansui, said 'The borderland of Yansui has none who can be recommended for the Erudite Learning and Elevated Literary Expression degree';
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dedi of Sichuan, acting as governor of Yansui, had said that 'on the Yansui frontier there was no one qualified to recommend for the Special Literary Examination';

sentences.zh: 少詹事邵遠平奏'南方人輕浮不可用'。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor Shao Yuanping memorialized 'southerners are frivolous and cannot be used.'
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor Shao Yuanping had memorialized that 'southerners are frivolous and unfit for office.'

sentences.zh: 朕心甚不愜，因皆罷斥。

translations.literal: My heart was greatly displeased, and for that reason all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: I was deeply displeased and dismissed them all.

sentences.zh: 今弘祚又以謬言陳奏，下部議降調。

translations.literal: Now Hongzuo again presents false words in memorial; the ministry is ordered to deliberate demotion and transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Now Hongzuo has again memorialized with such reckless words; refer the matter to the ministries for demotion.

sentences.zh: 」三十九年，命修高家堰河工，病卒。

translations.literal: " In the thirty-ninth year he was ordered to repair the Gaojia Embankment river works and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he was assigned to repair the Gaojia Embankment hydraulic works and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子絳，官至廣東布政使；

translations.literal: His son Jiang rose to provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong;
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiang rose to be provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong;

sentences.zh: 綱，初授兵部主事，累官湖南布政使，雍正間，擢雲南巡撫，疏劾署巡撫楊名時徇隱廢弛，籓庫借支未清款項至十九萬有奇，名時坐是得罪。

translations.literal: Zigang, first appointed clerk in the Ministry of War, rose through offices to provincial administration commissioner of Hunan; in the Yongzheng reign he was promoted to governor of Yunnan and memorialized impeaching Acting Governor Yang Mingshi for favoritism, concealment, and lax administration—the princely treasury's unpaid advances on loans amounted to more than one hundred and ninety thousand taels—and Yang Mingshi was punished for this.
translations.idiomatic: Zigang began as a clerk in the Ministry of War and rose to provincial administration commissioner of Hunan; in the Yongzheng era he was made governor of Yunnan and memorialized against Acting Governor Yang Mingshi for covering up misconduct and neglect—unpaid advances from the provincial treasury totaled more than 190,000 taels—and Yang Mingshi was punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 尋調撫福建，卒，諡勤恪。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to govern Fujian, died, and posthumous title Qinke (Diligent and Respectful).
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Fujian, died in office, and received the posthumous name Qinke ("Diligent and Respectful").

sentences.zh: 王騭，字辰岳，山東福山人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, styled Chenyue, was a man of Fushan in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, styled Chenyue, came from Fushan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi, appointed clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，典試廣東。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi he served as chief examiner in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kangxi he served as chief examiner for Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He served through bureau director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a bureau director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出為四川松威道。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as commissioner of the Songwei Circuit in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was sent out as intendant of the Songwei Circuit in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時徵雲南，騭督運軍糧，覆舟墜馬，屢經險阻，師賴以濟。

translations.literal: At the time the campaign was in Yunnan; Zhi supervised transport of army grain, capsized boats and fell from horses, repeatedly passed through dangers, and the army relied on this to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yunnan campaign he supervised military grain transport, surviving capsized boats and falls from horses through repeated perils, and the army depended on him to get supplies through.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，壘溪大定堡山後生番出掠，巡撫韓世琦檄兵追剿，令騭駐茂州，與總兵高鼎議剿撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the raw tribesmen behind Dading Fortress at Leixi came out raiding; Governor Han Shiqi dispatched troops to pursue and suppress, ordering Zhi to garrison at Maozhou and discuss suppression and appeasement with Regional Commander Gao Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year raw tribesmen beyond Dading Fortress at Leixi raided the border; Governor Han Shiqi sent troops in pursuit and stationed Zhi at Maozhou to plan pacification with Regional Commander Gao Ding.

sentences.zh: 騭赴堡開諭，番族據巴豬寨，陽就撫，負嵎如故。

translations.literal: Zhi went to the fort to proclaim and instruct; the tribes held Bazhu Stockade, outwardly submitting to appeasement while showing defiance as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi went to the fort to offer terms; the tribes held Bazhu Stockade, pretending to accept pacification while remaining defiant.

sentences.zh: 騭招撫附近諸​​寨，遣兵自廟山進，圍寨，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: Zhi summoned nearby stockades to appeasement, sent troops advancing from Miaoshan, besieged the stockade, and beheaded and captured beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He won over neighboring stockades, sent troops in from Miaoshan, besieged the stronghold, and killed or captured countless enemies.

sentences.zh: 追至黑水江，賊渠挖子被焚死，山後番眾悉降。

translations.literal: Pursuit reached the Heishui River; the bandit chief Wazi was burned to death, and all the tribesmen behind the mountains submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached the Blackwater River; the rebel leader Wazi was burned to death and all the tribes beyond the mountains surrendered.

sentences.zh: 調直隸口北道，未行。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Koubei Circuit in Zhili but had not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Koubei Circuit in Zhili but had not yet left.

sentences.zh: 時以太和殿工，命採蜀中柟木。

translations.literal: At the time, because of work on the Hall of Supreme Harmony, an order was issued to harvest nanmu timber in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Work on the Hall of Supreme Harmony required nanmu timber from Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 騭入覲，疏言：「四川大半環山巉岩，惟成都稍平衍。

translations.literal: Zhi entered audience and memorialized: "Sichuan for the most part is ringed by steep mountains and perilous cliffs; only Chengdu is somewhat level and open.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi came to court and memorialized: "Most of Sichuan is ringed by steep mountains; only Chengdu lies on relatively level ground.

sentences.zh: 巨材所生，必於深林窮壑，人跡罕到，斧斤難施，所以久存。

translations.literal: Where great timbers grow must be deep forests and remote ravines, places human tracks rarely reach where axe and saw are hard to apply—that is why they endure so long.
translations.idiomatic: The largest timber grows in deep forest and remote ravines where few people go and axes can scarcely reach—hence it survives.

sentences.zh: 民夫入山採木，足胝履穿，攀藤側立，施工既難；

translations.literal: When laborers enter the mountains to cut timber, feet grow callused and soles worn through; clinging to vines they stand sideways—the work is already difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Laborers who enter the mountains return with callused feet and torn shoes, clinging to vines on sheer cliffs—the cutting alone is grueling;

sentences.zh: 而運路自山抵江，或百餘裡，或七八十里，深澗急灘，溪流紆折，經時歷月，始至其地。

translations.literal: yet the transport route from mountain to river may be more than a hundred li or seventy or eighty li, with deep gorges and rapids, streams winding and bending—months pass before they reach the destination.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the haul from mountain to river may run over a hundred li or seventy or eighty li through deep gorges and rapids along winding streams, taking months to reach open water.

sentences.zh: 木在溪間，必待暴水而出，故陸運必於春冬，水運必於夏秋，非可一徑而行，計日而至，其艱如此。

translations.literal: Timber lies among streams and must await flood waters to float out; thus overland transport must be in spring and winter, water transport in summer and autumn—it cannot be one path straight through arriving by counted days; the hardship is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Logs stranded in streams must wait for floodwaters; land transport is possible only in spring and winter, water transport only in summer and autumn—not a single route that can be finished on a schedule. Such is the hardship.

sentences.zh: 且四川禍變相踵，荒煙百里。

translations.literal: Moreover Sichuan's disasters and rebellions followed one upon another; desolate smoke for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Sichuan has suffered one catastrophe after another until mile upon mile lies deserted.

sentences.zh: 臣當年運糧行間，滿目瘡痍。

translations.literal: When this minister in former years transported grain along the roads, what met the eye was scars of war.
translations.idiomatic: When I transported grain through the province years ago, every road showed the scars of war.

sentences.zh: 自蕩平以後，休養生息。

translations.literal: Since pacification there has been recuperation and growth of population.
translations.idiomatic: Since pacification the people have begun to recover.

sentences.zh: 然計通省戶口，仍不過一萬八千餘丁，不及他省一縣之眾。

translations.literal: Yet counting the whole province's registered households, they still do not exceed eighteen thousand-odd ding—less than a single county in other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the whole province counts barely eighteen thousand registered males—fewer than a single county elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 就中抽撥五千入山採木，衣糧器具，盈千累百，遣發民夫，遠至千里，近亦數百里，耕作全廢，國賦何徵？

translations.literal: From among them if five thousand are drafted to enter the mountains for timber, clothing, grain, and tools accumulate in thousands and hundreds; conscripted laborers are sent as far as a thousand li, as near as several hundred li—plowing is wholly abandoned; how can state taxes be levied?
translations.idiomatic: Draft five thousand of them for timber work, with thousands of sets of clothing, grain, and tools, and corvée sent as far as a thousand li or as near as several hundred li—all farming stops. How will land tax be collected?

sentences.zh: 請敕下撫臣，親詣採柟處察勘，量材取用，其必不能採運者，奏請上裁。

translations.literal: I ask that orders be sent down to the provincial governor to go in person to the nanmu-cutting sites to survey, use materials according to measure; those that certainly cannot be cut and transported—memorialize and request the emperor's decision.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the provincial governor be ordered to inspect the cutting sites in person, take only what can be used, and memorialize for the emperor's decision on timber that cannot possibly be harvested and transported.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上諭曰：「四川屢經兵火，困苦已極，採木累民。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived the emperor instructed: "Sichuan has repeatedly suffered warfare by fire; its distress has reached the extreme—timber cutting burdens the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the emperor said: "Sichuan has been repeatedly ravaged by war and its people are in extreme misery; timber-cutting only adds to their burden.

sentences.zh: 塞外松木，取充殿材，足支數百年，何必柟木？

translations.literal: Pine timber beyond the pass can be taken to serve as palace timber, enough to last several hundred years—why must it be nanmu?
translations.idiomatic: Pine from beyond the passes can serve for the palace for centuries—why insist on nanmu?

sentences.zh: 令免採運。

translations.literal: Order exemption from cutting and transport.
translations.idiomatic: Exempt Sichuan from cutting and transport.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，吏部循例疏請司道內擢京堂，騭未與，特命內升。

translations.literal: " Before long the Ministry of Personnel followed precedent memorializing inner promotion of circuit intendant to capital bureau chief; Zhi was not included, but a special order promoted him inward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon thereafter the Ministry of Personnel routinely proposed promoting circuit intendants to capital posts; Zhi was omitted, but the emperor specially ordered his promotion.

sentences.zh: 尋授光祿寺少卿，累遷太常寺卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was transferred through promotions to minister of the Court of Imperial Music.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and eventually rose to minister of the Court of Imperial Music.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，上諭曰：「大吏以操守為耍，大法則小廉，百姓蒙福。

translations.literal: At his audience of farewell the emperor instructed: "Great officials take integrity as essential; great law means small personal probity—the common people receive blessings."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor said: "Great officials must hold integrity paramount; uphold the greater law and petty graft will cease, and the people will prosper."

sentences.zh: 」騭對曰：「臣向在四川，不取民間粒米束草，日費取給於家。

translations.literal: " Zhi replied: "This minister formerly in Sichuan took not a grain of rice or bundle of straw from the people; daily expenses were supplied from home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied: "When I was in Sichuan I took not a grain of rice or blade of grass from the people; my daily expenses came from my own household."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「身為大臣，日費必取給於家，勢有所不能。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "As a great minister, daily expenses necessarily supplied from home—in situation there is what one cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "As a high minister you cannot entirely live off your own purse—that is scarcely possible.

sentences.zh: 但操守廉潔，念念愛民，便為良吏，且亦須安靜。

translations.literal: But with integrity and clean hands, every thought loving the people, then one is a good official; moreover one must also be tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: But if you keep your integrity, keep the people always in mind, and govern quietly, you will be a fine official.

sentences.zh: 貪污屬吏，先當訓誡；

translations.literal: Greedy and corrupt subordinate officials should first be admonished and instructed;
translations.idiomatic: For corrupt subordinates, admonish them first;

sentences.zh: 不悛，則糾劾。

translations.literal: if they do not reform, then impeach.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not reform, then impeach them."

sentences.zh: 」瀕行，賜帑金千。

translations.literal: " As he was about to depart, a thousand taels from the privy purse were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart the emperor bestowed a thousand taels from the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「江西自蕩平後，積年蠲免銀米二百萬有奇，民生漸裕。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Jiangxi since pacification has over the years been granted remissions of silver and grain totaling more than two million taels; the people's livelihood has gradually grown ample.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Since pacification Jiangxi has received tax remissions totaling more than two million taels in silver and grain, and livelihoods have gradually improved.

sentences.zh: 然徵收之弊，尚為民累，錢糧明加火​​耗，暗加重戥，部院司道府皆有解費。

translations.literal: Yet abuses in collection still burden the people: land-tax silver openly adds surcharges for melting, secretly adds weight to the scales; ministries, provincial offices, circuits, and prefectures all have delivery fees.
translations.idiomatic: Yet collection abuses still burden the people: open surcharges for melting fees and secret overweighting on the scales, with every level from ministry to prefecture charging 'delivery fees.'

sentences.zh: 臣入境之初，火耗已減，解費尚存，即揭示剔除積弊，盡革官役上下大小雜費。

translations.literal: When this minister first entered the province, melting surcharges had already been reduced but delivery fees remained; he immediately posted notices eliminating accumulated abuses and abolishing great and small miscellaneous fees throughout official and clerical ranks above and below.
translations.idiomatic: When I first arrived I had already cut melting surcharges, but delivery fees remained; I posted notices abolishing accumulated abuses and all miscellaneous fees at every level of officialdom.

sentences.zh: 南昌、新建二縣漕糧尚仍民兌，俱行革除，漕運積年陋規，搜剔無遺。

translations.literal: Nanchang and Xinjian two districts still had grain transport paid by the people by conversion; all were abolished; long-standing bad customs in grain transport were investigated and eliminated without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Nanchang and Xinjian still forced commoners to deliver grain transport in person—I abolished that practice and rooted out every longstanding abuse in the transport system.

sentences.zh: 但在民則省費，在官則失利。

translations.literal: Yet for the people this meant saving expense; for officials it meant loss of profit.
translations.idiomatic: The people saved money, but officials lost their illicit gains.

sentences.zh: 恐臣去後，空言無用，乞天語嚴禁，不致前弊復生。

translations.literal: He feared that after the minister departed empty words would be useless; he begged imperial words to forbid strictly lest former abuses revive.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that after I leave these reforms will vanish into empty talk; I beg Your Majesty to issue strict prohibitions so the old abuses do not return.

sentences.zh: 」下所司知之。

translations.literal: " The directive was sent down to the responsible offices to note.
translations.idiomatic: The court forwarded the memorial to the responsible agencies for implementation.

sentences.zh: 時湖廣叛卒夏逢龍據武昌，陷黃州。

translations.literal: At the time the mutinous soldier Xia Fenglong of Huguang held Wuchang and captured Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebel soldier Xia Fenglong in Huguang held Wuchang and had taken Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 騭次邵武，聞警，恐蔓及江西，奏撥福建兵協剿。

translations.literal: Zhi stopped at Shaowu, heard the alarm, feared spread to Jiangxi, and memorialized allocating Fujian troops for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was passing through Shaowu when he heard the alarm; fearing the rebellion might spread into Jiangxi, he memorialized to dispatch Fujian troops for joint suppression.

sentences.zh: 自海禁既弛，奸民雜入商販，出洋劫掠。

translations.literal: Since the maritime prohibition had been relaxed, scoundrels mingled with merchants and went to sea plundering.
translations.idiomatic: After the maritime ban was lifted, rogues mixed with merchants and went to sea as pirates.

sentences.zh: 騭既上官，即檄溫州總兵蔣懋勳、黃岩總兵林本植、定海總兵董大本以舟師出洋搜捕。

translations.literal: Once Zhi had taken office he immediately dispatched orders to Wenzhou Regional Commander Jiang Maoxun, Huangyan Regional Commander Lin Benzhi, and Dinghai Regional Commander Dong Daben to take naval forces to sea for search and capture.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office Zhi ordered Wenzhou Regional Commander Jiang Maoxun, Huangyan Regional Commander Lin Benzhi, and Dinghai Regional Commander Dong Daben to send fleets to search the seas.

sentences.zh: 懋勳、本植得賊舟七、大本於白沙灣獲巨艦一，斬盜渠楊仕玉等十六輩，釋被擄難民百十一人。

translations.literal: Maoxun and Benzhi obtained seven pirate vessels; Daben at Baisha Bay captured one great ship, beheaded the pirate leader Yang Shiyu and sixteen others, and released one hundred eleven persons among the populace who had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun and Benzhi seized seven pirate vessels; Daben captured a large ship at Baisha Bay, beheaded the pirate chief Yang Shiyu and fifteen others, and freed 111 kidnapped civilians.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上幸浙江，賜騭御用冠服。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor visited Zhejiang and bestowed on Zhi imperial-use cap and gown.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor toured Zhejiang and granted Zhi imperial court robes.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「爾任總督，實心任事，浙、閩黎庶稱爾清廉，故特加優賚。

translations.literal: He instructed: "You hold the post of governor-general, serving affairs with sincere heart; the common people of Zhe and Min call you clean-handed—for this reason special added favor is bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "As governor-general you have served conscientiously; the people of Zhejiang and Fujian praise your integrity, and for this I grant you special favor."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，召拜戶部尚書，以老病累疏乞休，詔輒慰留。

translations.literal: " Before long he was summoned and appointed minister of the Ministry of Revenue; because of old age and illness he repeatedly memorialized begging retirement, and edicts repeatedly comforted and detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as minister of the Ministry of Revenue; age and illness led him to memorialize repeatedly for retirement, but each time the emperor urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，召大學士、九卿及河督於成龍入對，上責成龍排陷靳輔，並及騭與左都御史董訥、內閣學士李應薦附和成龍，騭等具疏引罪，訥、應薦並奪官，騭原品休致。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year the emperor summoned Grand Secretaries, the Nine Ministers, and River Controller Yu Chenglong for audience; the emperor reproached Chenglong for plotting against Jin Fu and extended this to Zhi together with Censor-in-Chief Dong Ne and Grand Secretariat Academician Li Yingjian for echoing Chenglong; Zhi and others all submitted memorials confessing guilt; Ne and Yingjian were both stripped of office, while Zhi retired at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year the emperor summoned Grand Secretaries, the Nine Ministers, and River Controller Yu Chenglong; he accused Chenglong of framing Jin Fu and implicated Zhi, Censor-in-Chief Dong Ne, and Academician Li Yingjian for siding with Chenglong. Zhi and the others submitted confessions; Ne and Yingjian were dismissed, while Zhi was allowed to retire at his original rank.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，卒於家，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died at home and was granted sacrificial burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he died at home and was granted funeral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宋犖，字牧仲，河南商丘人，權子。

translations.literal: Song Luo, styled Muzhong, was a native of Shangqiu in Henan, son of Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Luo, styled Muzhong, came from Shangqiu in Henan and was the son of Song Quan.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，犖年十四，應詔以大臣子列侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, Luo being fourteen, he answered the edict and as a great minister's son was enrolled among the bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, at age fourteen, he answered an imperial summons and was enrolled among the guards as a minister's son.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，試授通判。

translations.literal: After a year, on examination he was appointed deputy prefect.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he passed an examination and was appointed deputy prefect.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，授湖廣黃州通判。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he was appointed deputy prefect of Huangzhou in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kangxi he was made deputy prefect of Huangzhou in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授理籓院院判，遷刑部員外郎，榷贛關，還遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed vice-director of the Court of Colonial Affairs, transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments, supervised the Gan customs monopoly, and on return was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became vice-director of the Court of Colonial Affairs, then transferred to the Ministry of Punishments as vice director, took charge of the Gan River customs, and on returning was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授直隸通永道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed intendant of the Tongyong Circuit in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was made intendant of the Tongyong Circuit in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷山東按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 再遷江蘇布政使，察司庫虧三十六萬有奇，犖揭報督撫，責前布政使劉鼎、章欽文分償。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to provincial treasurer of Jiangsu; he discovered the provincial treasury short by more than three hundred and sixty thousand taels, and Luo reported this to the governor-general and governor, holding the former treasurers Liu Ding and Zhang Qinwen responsible to repay in shares.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made provincial treasurer of Jiangsu and found the treasury short by more than 360,000 taels. Luo reported this to his superiors and held former treasurers Liu Ding and Zhang Qinwen liable to make restitution.

sentences.zh: 戶部採銅鑄錢，定值斤六分五釐，犖以江蘇不產銅，採自他省，值昂過半，牒巡撫田雯，疏請停採。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue collected copper to cast coin, fixing the price at six fen five li per jin; Luo, on the grounds that Jiangsu does not produce copper and must obtain it from other provinces at a cost more than half again as high, memorialized the governor Tian Wen and submitted a memorial requesting cessation of collection.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Revenue was buying copper for coinage at six fen five li per jin. Luo pointed out that Jiangsu produced no copper and had to import it at more than half again the official price; he wrote Governor Tian Wen and memorialized the throne to halt procurement.

sentences.zh: 下部議，改視各關例，斤一錢。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the ministries for deliberation; it was changed to follow the precedent of the various customs posts, one qian per jin.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and adopted the rate used at the customs posts—one qian per jin.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 湖廣叛卒夏逢龍為亂，徵江西兵赴剿，次九江，挾餉缺幾譁變。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldier Xia Fenglong of Huguang raised rebellion; Jiangxi troops were mobilized for suppression; halted at Jiujiang, they took advantage of pay shortages and nearly mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huguang mutineer Xia Fenglong rebelled, Jiangxi troops were called up for the campaign. They halted at Jiujiang, and with pay running short they nearly erupted in mutiny.

sentences.zh: 犖行次彭澤，聞報，檄發湖口庫帑充行糧，兵乃進。

translations.literal: Luo, traveling and stopping at Pengze, on hearing the report issued orders to disburse treasury funds at Hukou to serve as marching provisions, and the troops then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was passing through Pengze when he heard the news; he ordered funds from the Hukou treasury released as marching rations, and the troops moved on.

sentences.zh: 至南昌受事，舊裁督標兵李美玉、袁大相糾三千餘人，謀劫倉庫，應逢龍以叛。

translations.literal: On reaching Nanchang to assume office, the former dismissed governor's standard troops Li Meiyu and Yuan Daxiang mustered more than three thousand men, plotting to raid the warehouses and join Fenglong in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Nanchang to take office, dismissed governor's guards Li Meiyu and Yuan Daxiang rallied more than three thousand men to raid the warehouses and join Xia Fenglong's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 犖诇知之，捕得美玉、大相，眾恟恟。

translations.literal: Luo learned of it through investigation, seized Meiyu and Daxiang, and the crowd was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Luo uncovered the plot through informants, arrested Meiyu and Daxiang, and the mob grew restive.

sentences.zh: 犖令即斬以徇，諭眾受煽惑者皆貸不問，眾乃定。

translations.literal: Luo ordered them immediately beheaded as a warning, announced to the crowd that all who had been incited would be pardoned and not questioned, and the crowd then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Luo had them executed on the spot as an example, announced amnesty for anyone merely led astray, and the disturbance subsided.

sentences.zh: 江西採竹木，饒州供紫竹，南康、九江供檀、柟諸木，通省派供貓竹，名雖官捐，實為民累，犖疏請動支正帑採買。

translations.literal: Jiangxi collected bamboo and timber: Raozhou supplied purple bamboo, Nankang and Jiujiang supplied sandalwood, nanmu, and other woods; the whole province was assessed to supply mao bamboo—though nominally an official contribution, in fact it burdened the people; Luo memorialized requesting disbursement from the regular treasury for purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi levied bamboo and timber: Raozhou furnished purple bamboo, Nankang and Jiujiang sandalwood and nanmu, and the whole province mao bamboo. Though called an official levy, the cost fell on the people; Luo memorialized that purchases be made from the regular treasury instead.

sentences.zh: 上命歲終巡撫視察布政司庫，犖疏請糧驛道庫，布政使察覈；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that at year's end the governor inspect the provincial treasurer's treasury; Luo memorialized that grain-transport and courier circuit treasuries be inspected by the provincial treasurer;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered governors to inspect provincial treasuries at year's end; Luo proposed that grain-transport and courier circuit treasuries be audited by the provincial treasurer;

sentences.zh: 府庫，道員察覈。

translations.literal: prefectural treasuries, by circuit intendants.
translations.idiomatic: and prefectural treasuries by circuit intendants.

sentences.zh: 漢軍文武官吏受代，家屬例當還旗，經過州縣，點驗取結。

translations.literal: When civil and military officials of the Han Banners were relieved, their families by precedent had to return to the banners; passing through prefectures and districts they were checked and required to obtain certificates.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Banner officials completed their terms, their families were required to return to the banners; at every prefecture and district along the way they were inspected and made to obtain clearance certificates.

sentences.zh: 犖曰：「是以罪人待之也。

translations.literal: Luo said: "This is treating them like criminals.
translations.idiomatic: Luo said, "This treats them like criminals.

sentences.zh: 」疏請自贓私斥革並侵挪帑項解部比追外，止給到京定限咨文，俾示區別。

translations.literal: " He memorialized that apart from those dismissed for corruption and those whose embezzled funds sent to the ministry were being pursued for comparison and recovery, only a dispatch with a fixed deadline for reaching the capital should be issued, so as to show a distinction.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized that except for officials dismissed for corruption or whose embezzled funds were being recovered by the ministry, returning families should receive only a travel pass with a deadline for reaching the capital, to mark the distinction.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were sent down to the ministries for deliberation and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All were referred to the ministries, approved, and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，調江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 蘇州濱海各縣遇颶，上元、六合諸縣發山水，淮、揚、徐屬縣河溢，疏請視被災輕重，蠲減如例。
