translations.literal: Coastal counties of Suzhou suffered typhoons; Shangyuan, Liuhe, and other counties were struck by mountain floods; counties subordinate to Huai, Yang, and Xu circuits had rivers overflow; he memorialized requesting remissions according to precedent, in proportion to the severity of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Typhoons struck the coastal counties of Suzhou; mountain floods hit Shangyuan, Liuhe, and neighboring counties; rivers overflowed throughout the Huai, Yang, and Xu circuits. He memorialized for tax remissions scaled to the severity of each disaster, as precedent allowed.

sentences.zh: 發江寧、鳳陽倉儲米麥散賑。

translations.literal: He released grain and wheat from the Jiangning and Fengyang storehouses for relief distribution.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Jiangning and Fengyang granaries and distributed rice and wheat as relief.

sentences.zh: 別疏請除太湖傍坍地賦額，戶部以地逾千畝，令詳察。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he requested removal of tax quotas on collapsed land beside Tai Lake; the Board of Revenue, on the grounds that the land exceeded a thousand mu, ordered detailed investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he asked to cancel tax assessments on land washed away beside Lake Tai. The Board of Revenue, noting the area exceeded a thousand mu, ordered a detailed investigation.

sentences.zh: 犖再疏上陳，上特允之。

translations.literal: Luo memorialized again setting forth the facts, and the emperor specially approved.
translations.idiomatic: Luo memorialized again, and the emperor granted his request as a special favor.

sentences.zh: 犖在江蘇，三遇上南巡，嘉犖居官安靜，迭蒙賞賚，以犖年逾七十，書「福」、「壽」字以賜。

translations.literal: While Luo was in Jiangsu he thrice encountered the emperor's southern tours; the emperor praised Luo's quiet conduct in office and repeatedly bestowed rewards; as Luo had passed seventy, the emperor wrote the characters "Fortune" and "Longevity" to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: During Luo's tenure in Jiangsu the emperor made three southern tours, praised his steady and unassuming conduct, and showered him with rewards. When Luo passed seventy, the emperor wrote the characters for "fortune" and "longevity" and presented them as gifts.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，擢吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，以老乞罷，瀕行，賜以詩。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, on grounds of age he requested dismissal; as he was about to depart, a poem was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he asked to retire on account of age; as he was about to leave, the emperor presented him with a poem.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，詣京師祝聖壽，加太子少師，复賜以詩，還裡。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he went to the capital to congratulate the emperor on his birthday, was given the additional title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, again received a bestowed poem, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he traveled to the capital for the emperor's birthday celebration, was named Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, received another imperial poem, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty and was granted sacrificial burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was granted state funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 陳詵，字叔大，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Shen, styled Shuda, was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shen, styled Shuda, came from Haining in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年舉人，授中書科中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi he passed the provincial examination and was appointed secretary in the Secretariat Section of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in the eleventh year of Kangxi and was appointed a secretarial clerk in the Secretariat Section.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，考授吏科給事中，乞養歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, on examination he was appointed supervising secretary of the Personnel Section and requested leave to return home to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he passed an examination for the post of supervising secretary in the Personnel Section, then asked leave to return home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，起補原官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was recalled to fill his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 輔刑科掌印給事中。

translations.literal: He assisted as seal-holding supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting seal-holding supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「淮、黃自古不兩行。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The Huai and the Yellow Rivers from antiquity have not flowed together.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The Huai and Yellow Rivers have never run together—this is an ancient truth.

sentences.zh: 邇者修歸仁堤，開胡家溝，出睢湖之水；

translations.literal: Recently the Guiren embankment was repaired and the Hujia Ditch opened to discharge the waters of the Sui Lake;
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Guiren embankment was repaired and the Hujia Ditch opened to drain Sui Lake;

sentences.zh: 閉六壩，加築高家堰，出洪澤湖之水。

translations.literal: the six barrages were closed and the Gaojia Weir heightened and strengthened to discharge the waters of Hongze Lake.
translations.idiomatic: the six barrages were closed and the Gaojia Weir raised to channel Hongze Lake.

sentences.zh: 此借淮敵黃不易之理。

translations.literal: This applies the principle that the Huai is borrowed to contend with the Yellow River—a change not easily made.
translations.idiomatic: This applies the old principle of pitting the Huai against the Yellow—a difficult and risky expedient.

sentences.zh: 然淮水入運者多，則敵黃仍弱。

translations.literal: Yet if much Huai water enters the Grand Canal, then the contention with the Yellow is still weak.
translations.idiomatic: But when too much Huai water is diverted into the Grand Canal, the Huai's power to hold back the Yellow is weakened.

sentences.zh: 舊設天妃閘，自淮、黃交會處至清江浦，凡為五閘，重運到時，更迭啟閉，過即下板鎖斷，是以全淮注黃。

translations.literal: Formerly the Tianfei sluice-gates were established—from where the Huai and Yellow meet to Qingjiangpu there were five gates in all; when grain transport arrived they were opened and closed in rotation, and once passage was complete the boards were lowered to seal them shut, so that the whole Huai was poured into the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: The old Tianfei sluices ran from the Huai–Yellow confluence to Qingjiangpu—five gates in all. During the grain transport season they opened in rotation and closed again once the barges passed, directing the full force of the Huai into the Yellow.

sentences.zh: 其引入運河者，不過暫資濟運。

translations.literal: What was led into the Grand Canal was only to assist transport temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: Water sent into the Grand Canal was only a temporary aid to shipping.

sentences.zh: 自改建草壩，淮、黃盡趨運河，清江浦民居可危。

translations.literal: Since the reconstruction as earthen barrages, the Huai and Yellow both rush entirely toward the Grand Canal, and the dwellings of Qingjiangpu are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Since the sluices were rebuilt as earthen barrages, both rivers pour into the Grand Canal, putting the homes of Qingjiangpu in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 宜复天妃閘舊制，使淮易敵黃，有裨大工。

translations.literal: The Tianfei sluice-gate old system should be restored, so that the Huai may readily contend with the Yellow, to the benefit of the great works.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianfei sluices should be restored to their former design so the Huai can once again hold back the Yellow—this would greatly aid the river-control project.

sentences.zh: 」疏下河督張鵬翮議行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to River Controller Zhang Penghe for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to River Controller Zhang Penghe, who approved and carried it out.

sentences.zh: 尋疏劾山東蒲台知縣俞宏聲以赦前細故，拘系監生王觀成，迫令自殺；

translations.literal: Soon after he memorialized impeaching Yu Hongsheng, magistrate of Putai in Shandong, for on a trifling matter before the amnesty imprisoning the student Wang Guancheng and forcing him to commit suicide;
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized against Yu Hongsheng, magistrate of Putai in Shandong, who over a petty pre-amnesty dispute had imprisoned the student Wang Guancheng and driven him to suicide;

sentences.zh: 巡撫王國昌僅以杖責解役結案，玩視民命。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Guochang had only punished with the bamboo staff and dismissed the runners to close the case, treating the people's lives lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Guochang had merely caned the bailiffs and closed the case, showing contempt for human life.

sentences.zh: 命侍郎吳涵偕詵往按，宏聲坐奪官，國昌等議處。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wu Han was ordered to accompany Shen on an investigation; Hongsheng was stripped of office on conviction, and Guochang and others were subject to deliberation on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wu Han was sent with Shen to investigate. Hongsheng was dismissed from office; Guochang and others were referred for disciplinary action.

sentences.zh: 授鴻臚寺卿，再遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of the Court of State Ceremonial, then again transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Court of State Ceremonial, then promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，授貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was appointed governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was appointed governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「貴州田地俱在層岡峻嶺間，土性寒涼，收成歉薄，人牛種蓺維艱。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Guizhou fields all lie among tiered ridges and steep peaks; the soil is cold in nature and yields are meager; for men and oxen to plant crops is exceedingly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Guizhou's farmland lies on steep, terraced slopes where the soil is cold and poor and harvests are thin; both farmers and oxen struggle to bring land under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 前撫臣王蓺因合屬田地荒蕪十之四五，減輕舊則，招徠開墾成熟，六年後起科。

translations.literal: The former governor Wang Yi, because throughout the jurisdiction four or five tenths of the fields lay waste, reduced the old tax rates, recruited settlers to open and cultivate until maturity, and levied taxes after six years.
translations.idiomatic: Former governor Wang Yi, finding four or five tenths of the land in his jurisdiction lying fallow, reduced the old tax rates, encouraged settlers to reclaim and cultivate the land, and deferred taxation for six years after fields were brought into production.

sentences.zh: 有續報者亦如之。

translations.literal: Those who reported subsequently were treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent reports received the same treatment.

sentences.zh: 」疏下部，如所請。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the ministries, and as requested was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries and approved as requested.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，調湖北。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 疏劾布政使王毓賢虧帑，命解任。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Provincial Treasurer Wang Yuxian for treasury deficits and was ordered to relieve him of office.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against Provincial Treasurer Wang Yuxian for treasury shortfalls, and Wang was ordered to step down.

sentences.zh: 尋以盤驗已完，奏免其罪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on the grounds that the audit was complete, he memorialized to exempt him from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the audit was completed, he memorialized that Wang be cleared of wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 五十年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，乞休，命致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he requested retirement and was ordered to retire with honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he asked to retire and was granted honorable retirement.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，卒，賜祭葬，諡清恪。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he died and was granted sacrificial burial, posthumous title Qingke.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he died and was granted state funeral rites, with the posthumous epithet Qingke (Pure and Reverent).

sentences.zh: 子世倌，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Shichang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen Shichang has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：當三籓亂時，雲、貴、閩、粵，其發難地也；

translations.literal: The commentary states: At the time of the Three Feudatories rebellion, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, and Guangdong were where the trouble arose;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: During the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, and Guangdong were where the uprising began;

sentences.zh: 蹂躪所及，湖南北、江西、四川，受害最甚。

translations.literal: where the ravaging reached, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, and Sichuan suffered most severely.
translations.idiomatic: but Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, and Sichuan, where the armies marched, suffered the worst devastation.

sentences.zh: 伊闢、王繼文撫雲南，從師而南，參與軍畫，其事已別見；

translations.literal: Yang Yongjian and Wang Jiwen as governors of Yunnan followed the army south and took part in military planning—their affairs are recorded elsewhere;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yongjian and Wang Jiwen governed Yunnan, marched south with the armies, and took part in military planning—their careers are told elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 雍建於貴州，締虞於四川，弘祚於廣東，騭於江西，犖承騭，詵遙繼雍建，兵後撫綏甚勤。

translations.literal: Yongjian in Guizhou, Dingu in Sichuan, Hongzuo in Guangdong, Zhi in Jiangxi—Luo succeeded Zhi, and Shen in turn followed Yongjian from afar in time; after the armies they pacified and comforted with great diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yongjian in Guizhou, Yao Dingu in Sichuan, Zhu Hongzuo in Guangdong, and Wang Zhi in Jiangxi—Song Luo succeeded Wang Zhi, and Chen Shen in turn followed Yang Yongjian's path; all labored tirelessly to restore order after the war.

sentences.zh: 大亂方定，起衰救弊，出水火，登袵席，偉哉諸人之功歟！

translations.literal: Great chaos had just been settled; they raised what was declining and rescued what was failing, brought people out of fire and water and set them on the mat and coverlet—how great are these men's achievements!
translations.idiomatic: When the great rebellion had barely ended, they revived devastated provinces, rescued the people from misery, and restored them to peace and comfort—how magnificent their service was!
